key_insight: A non-neural machine learning pipeline can act as a "teacher" to train a compact neural network student that reproduces the pipeline's behavior, enabling end-to-end neural replacement of complex, heterogeneous ML systems.
problem_solved: How to convert bulky, non-differentiable or heterogeneous ML pipelines into a single, deployable neural model that preserves behavior while reducing maintenance, latency, and deployment complexity.
method: Treat the existing pipeline as a teacher: run inputs through the pipeline to generate soft targets and (optionally) intermediate representations for supervision.

Design a student neural network (architecture can mirror pipeline structure or be compact/efficient) and train it with losses that combine mimicry of teacher outputs and any available ground-truth labels.
Handle non-differentiable or specialized steps by supervising intermediate outputs, using surrogate differentiable approximations, or distilling behavior via dataset augmentation and loss weighting.
impact: Enables practitioners to replace fragile, multi-component ML pipelines with a single neural model that is easier to optimize, accelerate (hardware/quantization), and deploy to production or edge devices without large accuracy loss.

paper_title: Neural Network Conversion of Machine Learning Pipelines
paper_authors: Man-Ling Sung, Jan Silovsky, Man-Hung Siu, Herbert Gish, Chinnu Pittapally
